queries.hook: I can't stop overthinking. Inside, my mind won't settle, and I don't know how to carry it.
queries.diagnose: The untrained mind runs like the wind, replaying and imagining; left to itself it becomes its own enemy.
queries.steady: The mind can be trained slowly, by practice and letting go; each time it wanders, it can be gently brought back.

hook.speaker: Arjuna
hook.setting: Arjuna confesses the mind is as hard to hold as the wind; Krishna answers.
hook.sanskrit: चञ्चलं हि मनः कृष्ण प्रमाथि बलवद्दृढम् । तस्याहं निग्रहं मन्ये वायोरिव सुदुष्करम् ॥
hook.line: The mind is restless, stormy, stubborn and strong. Holding it feels like holding the wind.
hook.translation: For the mind is restless, Krishna, turbulent, powerful and stubborn. I think it is as hard to hold as the wind.
hook.why: The mind is hard to hold, but practice and letting go train it.

prasang.summary: Arjuna says the mind is restless, stormy and stubborn. Krishna agrees, and says practice and letting go can train it.
prasang.lesson: The mind is hard to hold, but practice and letting go train it.

alternates.speaker: Arjuna
alternates.setting: Krishna answers Arjuna, who asks why he must act at all if understanding is higher.
alternates.sanskrit: व्यामिश्रेणेव वाक्येन बुद्धिं मोहयसीव मे । तदेकं वद निश्चित्य येन श्रेयोऽहमाप्नुयाम् ॥
alternates.line: Your advice sounds mixed and confuses me. Tell me the one thing I should do.
alternates.translation: With these seemingly mixed words you confuse my mind. Tell me decisively that one thing by which I may reach the highest good.
alternates.why: Not acting is still a choice; do the work that is yours.

prasang.title: Why doing your duty without attachment is better
prasang.summary: Arjuna is confused and asks for one clear answer. Krishna says no one can stop acting, that repressing the body while the mind indulges is self-deception, and that action beats inaction.
prasang.lesson: Not acting is still a choice; do the work that is yours.

alternates.speaker: Krishna
alternates.setting: Krishna teaches Arjuna how to meditate and what a settled mind is like.
alternates.sanskrit: यतो यतो निश्चरति मनश्चञ्चलमस्थिरम् । ततस्ततो नियम्यैतदात्मन्येव वशं नयेत् ॥
alternates.line: Wherever the restless mind wanders, gently bring it back. Again and again.
alternates.translation: Wherever the restless, unsteady mind wanders, from there one should draw it back and bring it under the control of the self.
alternates.why: Moderation and gentle return, again and again, settle the mind.

prasang.title: Meditation in detail
prasang.summary: Krishna describes meditation: moderation in food and sleep, the mind like a lamp in a windless place, bringing the wandering mind back, and feeling others' joy and pain as one's own.
prasang.lesson: Moderation and gentle return, again and again, settle the mind.

verse.speaker: Nidagha
verse.sanskrit: इतश्चेतश्च सुव्यग्रं व्यर्थमेवाभिधावति । मनो दूरतरं याति ग्रामे कौलेयको यथा ॥
verse.line: The mind runs here and there for nothing, wandering far like a stray village dog.
verse.translation: The mind runs here and there, restless and pointless; it wanders far away, like a dog in a village.
verse.why: Naming how restless your mind is, is where peace begins.

prasang.title: Nidagha's lament
prasang.summary: Young Nidagha returns from pilgrimage disillusioned and pours out his heart to his teacher Ribhu: life is fleeting, the mind runs like a stray dog, craving gnaws every good quality, and mastering the mind is harder than drinking the ocean.
prasang.lesson: Naming how restless your mind is, is where peace begins.

verse.for_you: Your mind is the stray dog. It is not a moral failure, just a habit that was never trained. You asked for the pattern, and here it is: the restlessness is the running itself. You do not have to catch it.
verse.try_today: Watch where your mind wanders for ten minutes without pulling it back.
verse.scene_line: You are the young pilgrim, home from the road, and the dog is running again.
asks: How do I see the running without feeding it?

verse.speaker: Kalakavrikshiya
verse.setting: The sage closes his consolation of the deposed prince Kshemadarshi.
verse.sanskrit: महाह्रदः संक्षुभित आत्मनैव प्रसीदति / एवं नरः स्वात्मनैव कृतप्रज्ञः प्रसीदति ॥
verse.line: A churned-up lake settles and clears on its own. So does a mind, given time.
verse.translation: A great lake that has been churned up settles and clears by itself. In the same way a person who has gained wisdom becomes clear by himself.
verse.why: Grief can't restore what's gone. Want what's within reach, and let others' success be.

prasang.title: Kalakavrikshiya consoles the fallen prince
prasang.summary: Prince Kshemadarshi has lost his kingdom and wealth. The sage Kalakavrikshiya tells him grief has no power to restore what is gone, to want what is within reach, and to make peace with others' good fortune.
prasang.lesson: Grief can't restore what's gone. Want what's within reach, and let others' success be.

verse.for_you: Bring the mind back each time it wanders, with practice and letting go; make the mind your friend through steady practice.

verse.speaker: Bhushunda
verse.setting: Bhushunda, the ancient crow who has watched the ages pass, tells Vasishtha why he lives long and well.
verse.sanskrit: न भूतं न भविष्यं च चिन्तयामि कदाचन । दृष्टिमालम्ब्य तिष्ठामि वर्तमानामिहात्मना ॥
verse.line: I don't brood over the past or the future. I keep my attention on now.
verse.translation: I never brood over the past or the future. I hold my attention on the present, here, with myself.
verse.why: A long, steady life comes from a mind that stays in the present, wants little and stays kind.

prasang.title: Bhushunda, the crow who outlived the ages
prasang.summary: Vasishtha travels to a wish-fulfilling tree on Mount Meru to meet Bhushunda, a crow who has watched world-ages come and go. Asked how he has lived so long, untroubled, Bhushunda lists his habits: he doesn't brood on the past or future, doesn't fret about what he'll get next, doesn't grow arrogant from knowing, and shares in others' joys and sorrows.
prasang.story_hook: High on a mountain lived a crow who had watched whole ages of the world rise and fall.
prasang.lesson: A long, steady life comes from a mind that stays in the present, wants little and stays kind.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Arjuna asks which devotee is best; Krishna offers a ladder of practices.
verse.line: Practice is good, understanding better, meditation better still. But letting go of results brings peace at once.
verse.translation: Knowledge is better than mere practice; meditation is better than knowledge; giving up the fruit of action is better than meditation. From that renunciation, peace follows immediately.
verse.why: If the ideal is too hard, take the next step down, and keep going.
verse.misuse: Not 'stop caring how things turn out'. Peace comes from releasing the grip, not from indifference.

prasang.title: Form or formless: which devotee is best, and the ways to reach him
prasang.summary: Krishna says devotion to a personal form is easier, then offers a ladder: fix your mind; if not, practise; if not, work for me; if not, let go of results. Letting go brings peace at once.
prasang.lesson: If the ideal is too hard, take the next step down, and keep going.

verse.meaning: Krishna tells Arjuna that understanding is better than practice, and meditation better than understanding. But if those feel too difficult, the next step is to let go of the results of your actions. When you stop holding onto what you will get, peace arrives right away.
verse.for_you: You are trying to build something new while also caring for your parents, and the weight of how it will turn out keeps your mind spinning. The teaching says that if you cannot stop the thoughts, you can loosen the grip on the outcome.
verse.scene_line: You are standing at the edge of a ladder, unsure which rung to take next.
asks: How do I let go without becoming careless?
Is the peace I want waiting at the bottom of the ladder?
What does my work look like when I stop holding the outcome?

verse.speaker: Ribhu
verse.setting: Ribhu on inner stillness in an active life.
verse.sanskrit: बहिःकृत्रिमसंरंभो हृदि संरम्भवर्जितः । कर्ता बहिरकर्तान्तर्लोके विहर शुद्धधीः ॥
verse.line: Be busy on the outside and unhurried inside. Act fully, but don't let it agitate you.
verse.translation: Outwardly busy, inwardly free of agitation; a doer on the outside, a non-doer within: move through the world with a clear mind.
verse.why: Live fully in the world while staying unhurried inside.

prasang.title: How a free person lives
prasang.summary: Ribhu describes how a free person lives among others: letting go of what is lost, taking up what comes, doing the work at hand, speaking gently, busy outside and calm inside, and treating the whole world as family.
prasang.lesson: Live fully in the world while staying unhurried inside.

verse.meaning: Ribhu is telling Nidagha how a person who is free inside lives among others. Ribhu says to let go of what is lost and take up what comes. Do the work in front of you, speak gently, and treat the whole world as family. The mind stays calm inside even when the hands are busy. It is a state of being busy on the outside and unhurried inside.
verse.for_you: You are building your work and caring for your parents, and the mind wants to run ahead to every possible outcome. The teaching is not to stop the doing, but to let the doing stop agitating the mind.
verse.try_today: Do one small task with full attention and notice if the mind stays busy inside.
verse.scene_line: You are busy with your work, but the question is how to stay unhurried inside.
asks: How do I let go of the results while still caring for my parents?
Can I be busy outside without the mind running ahead?
How do I stop the mind from agitating me while I study?

story.title: King Janaka overhears the sages and keeps ruling, with a free mind
story.story_hook: One spring morning, a king out for a walk overheard a song that he could not stop thinking about.
story.summary: Walking in his spring garden, King Janaka overhears hidden sages singing about the self. Shaken, he climbs to his palace roof and questions everything he has lived for. When his doorkeeper calls him to the day's work, he decides not to run away: he gets up and does his duties, but with a mind that no longer clutches.
story.lesson: You don't have to leave your life to change it. Do the day's work with a mind that doesn't clutch.

anchor.speaker: Janaka
anchor.setting: King Janaka, alone on his palace roof after overhearing wandering sages, rethinks his life.
anchor.sanskrit: संपदश्च विचित्रा यास्ताश्चेच्चित्तेन संमताः । तत्ता अपि महारम्भा हन्त मन्ये महापदः ॥ आपदोऽपि विचित्रा यास्ताश्चेन्मनसि संमताः । तत्ता अपि महारम्भा मन्ये मनसि संपदः ॥
anchor.line: Good fortune the mind clutches becomes trouble. Trouble the mind accepts becomes a kind of fortune.
anchor.translation: All those dazzling fortunes, if the mind clings to them, are really great calamities in grand disguise. And all those varied misfortunes, if the mind accepts them, are really fortunes.
anchor.why: You don't have to leave your life to change it. Do the day's work with a mind that doesn't clutch.
anchor.misuse: Accepting a hardship doesn't mean not fixing what can be fixed.
